stances.claim: The current retirement age of 65 was set 122 years ago when life expectancy was 37; today's 70-year-olds are the equivalent of yesterday's 50-year-olds, and retirement ages should reflect this.
The 'amortal' ideal -- staying involved, pursuing aspirations, treating retirement as a change of tires for a new journey -- is the secret to adding life to years, not years to life.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban endorses Sen. Miriam Defensor-Santiago's Senate Bill 2797 extending government workers' retirement age from 65 to 70, noting the bill should have included the private sector and military (the judiciary is constitutionally fixed at 70 and cannot be changed by statute). He grounds the endorsement in actuarial data: current retirement ages were set 122 years ago when life expectancy was 37; today we live 30 years longer than our grandparents; scientific data show life expectancy rising 2-5 years per decade; today's 70-year-olds are the equivalent of yesterday's 50-year-olds. He surveys the science: adult stem cells (without embryonic-ethics controversy) point toward cures for diabetes, Alzheimer's, and certain cancers; resveratrol (in red grapes) restricts caloric absorption to lengthen life; and telomerase lengthens telomeres to immortalize human cells. The ideal is to be 'amortal' -- a Time magazine coinage for staying vital beyond conventional age limits through continued purpose and involvement ('retirement = change of tires for a new journey'). At a Makati cocktail reception he hosted for newly appointed Foreign Secretary Albert del Rosario and Ambassador Manolo Lopez, he toasted them as paradigm amortals: del Rosario (70+) climbed 20 stories in a Singapore blackout during the Aquino state visit, plays golf by walking the full 6 km without a cart, and previously sat on 40+ corporate boards; Lopez personally visited the Japan earthquake/tsunami disaster site despite radiation risks to supervise OFW relief. Other amortals at the reception: Ramos, Gokongwei, Oscar Lopez, George Ty, and Washington SyCip, plus 45 ambassadors including Liu Jianchao (China) and Stephen Lillie (UK).
